title: CBSE CLASS 12 — English | Voice Active Passive
description: Subject-wise test on Voice Active Passive (English) for CBSE CLASS 12. 50Q.
subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice transformation for the sentence: 'The children ate all the cookies.'

options.text: All the cookies are eaten by the children.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'are eaten' uses present tense, while the original sentence is in past tense.

options.text: All the cookies were eaten by the children.
options.explanation: Correct because it uses the simple past passive structure 'were + past participle'.

options.text: The children were eaten by all the cookies.
options.explanation: Incorrect because it reverses the subject and object, making the sentence illogical.

options.text: All the cookies had been eaten by the children.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'had been eaten' uses past perfect tense, which is not required here.

questions.explanation: The original sentence is in the simple past tense (ate). In passive voice, the structure for simple past is 'was/were + past participle'. 'Cookies' is plural, so 'were eaten' is correct.
questions.hint: Identify the tense of the original sentence and apply the passive voice structure accordingly.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Transform the following sentence into passive voice: 'The gardener is watering the plants.'

options.text: The plants are watered by the gardener.
options.explanation: Incorrect because it uses simple present passive, not present continuous.

options.text: The plants were being watered by the gardener.
options.explanation: Incorrect because it uses past continuous passive, not present continuous.

options.text: The plants are being watered by the gardener.
options.explanation: Correct because it uses the present continuous passive structure 'are being watered'.

options.text: The plants will be watered by the gardener.
options.explanation: Incorrect because it uses future simple passive, not present continuous.

questions.explanation: The original sentence is in the present continuous tense (is watering). The passive structure for present continuous is 'is/am/are + being + past participle'. 'Plants' is plural, so 'are being watered' is correct.
questions.hint: Identify the tense and structure of the original sentence before transforming it.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Select the correct passive voice form of the sentence: 'You must obey your parents.'

options.text: Your parents must be obeyed.
options.explanation: Grammatically correct but omits the agent 'you', making it less complete.

options.text: Your parents must be obeyed by you.
options.explanation: Correct because it includes the agent 'by you', making the transformation complete.

options.text: Your parents are obeyed by you.
options.explanation: Incorrect because it uses simple present passive, not modal verb structure.

options.text: Your parents should be obeyed by you.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'should' changes the meaning of the original sentence.

questions.explanation: The original sentence uses a modal verb 'must'. The passive structure for modal verbs is 'modal + be + past participle'. Both A and B are grammatically correct, but B retains the agent, which is generally preferred if the agent is specific, making it a more complete transformation.
questions.hint: Remember that modal verbs like 'must' require 'be' in the passive voice.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Choose the option that correctly transforms the sentence into passive voice: 'She has completed the assignment.'

options.text: The assignment is completed by her.
options.explanation: Incorrect because it uses simple present passive, not present perfect.

options.text: The assignment was completed by her.
options.explanation: Incorrect because it uses simple past passive, not present perfect.

options.text: The assignment has been completed by her.
options.explanation: Correct because it uses the present perfect passive structure 'has been completed'.

options.text: The assignment had been completed by her.
options.explanation: Incorrect because it uses past perfect passive, not present perfect.

questions.explanation: The original sentence is in the present perfect tense (has completed). The passive structure for present perfect is 'has/have + been + past participle'. 'Assignment' is singular, so 'has been completed' is correct.
questions.hint: Identify the tense of the original sentence and apply the passive voice structure accordingly.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Transform the imperative sentence into passive voice: 'Open the window.'

options.text: The window is opened.
options.explanation: Incorrect because it uses simple present passive, not the imperative passive structure.

options.text: You are requested to open the window.
options.explanation: Grammatically correct but implies a request rather than a direct command.

options.text: Let the window be opened.
options.explanation: Correct because it uses the imperative passive structure 'Let + object + be + past participle'.

options.text: The window should be opened.
options.explanation: Incorrect because it uses 'should', which changes the meaning to a suggestion rather than a command.

questions.explanation: For direct imperative sentences, the passive voice is commonly formed using 'Let + object + be + past participle'. Option B is also correct but implies a request, whereas 'Let' directly transforms the command.
questions.hint: Imperative sentences in passive voice often use 'Let' as the starting word.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Identify the correct passive voice transformation for the sentence: 'He gave me a book.'

options.text: A book was given to me by him.
options.explanation: Grammatically correct but not the only correct option.

options.text: I was given a book by him.
options.explanation: Grammatically correct but not the only correct option.

options.text: Both A and B
options.explanation: Correct because both transformations are grammatically valid.

options.text: Neither A nor B
options.explanation: Incorrect because both A and B are grammatically correct.

questions.explanation: This sentence has two objects: 'me' (indirect object) and 'a book' (direct object). Either can become the subject of the passive sentence. If 'a book' is the subject: 'A book was given to me by him.' If 'I' (from 'me') is the subject: 'I was given a book by him.' Both are correct.
questions.hint: Sentences with two objects can have two passive transformations.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice form of the sentence: 'The committee looked into the matter thoroughly.'

options.text: The matter was looked thoroughly into by the committee.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the adverb 'thoroughly' is misplaced.

options.text: The matter was looked into thoroughly by the committee.
options.explanation: Correct because the phrasal verb 'looked into' is kept intact and the adverb is correctly placed.

options.text: The matter thoroughly was looked into by the committee.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the adverb is misplaced before the verb phrase.

options.text: The matter is looked into thoroughly by the committee.
options.explanation: Incorrect because it uses present tense, while the original sentence is in past tense.

questions.explanation: The original sentence is in the simple past tense (looked into). The phrasal verb 'looked into' must be kept together in the passive voice. The adverb 'thoroughly' should logically follow the verb phrase.
questions.hint: Phrasal verbs must remain intact in passive voice transformations.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Transform the following into passive voice: 'Who wrote this letter?'

options.text: By whom was this letter written?
options.explanation: Grammatically correct but not the only correct option.

options.text: This letter was written by whom?
options.explanation: Grammatically correct but not listed as an option.

options.text: Who was this letter written by?
options.explanation: Grammatically correct but not the only correct option.

options.text: Both A and C
options.explanation: Correct because both transformations are grammatically valid.

questions.explanation: When 'Who' is the subject of an active interrogative sentence, its passive form usually begins with 'By whom' or ends with 'by whom/who'. Both 'By whom was this letter written?' and 'Who was this letter written by?' are grammatically correct and accepted forms.
questions.hint: Interrogative sentences in passive voice can start with 'By whom' or end with 'by whom/who'.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): The passive voice of 'They believe that he is innocent' is 'It is believed that he is innocent.' Reason (R): When the active voice has a reporting verb followed by a 'that' clause, the passive voice can be formed by beginning with 'It is + past participle of reporting verb + that clause'.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Correct because both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the reason does explain the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Incorrect because both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Incorrect because the assertion is true.

questions.explanation: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true. Assertion (A) provides a correct example of a passive transformation for a sentence with a reporting verb and a 'that' clause. Reason (R) correctly describes the rule for forming such passive sentences, thereby providing the correct explanation for Assertion (A).
questions.hint: Evaluate both the assertion and the reason separately before determining their relationship.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice transformation for the given sentence: 'She will finish the work by evening.'

options.text: The work will be finished by evening.
options.explanation: Grammatically correct but omits the agent 'by her'.

options.text: The work will be finished by her by evening.
options.explanation: Correct because it includes the agent 'by her' and maintains the original tense.

options.text: The work would be finished by her by evening.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'would' changes the tense to conditional, not future.

options.text: The work is finished by her by evening.
options.explanation: Incorrect because it uses present tense, not future.

questions.explanation: The original sentence is in the simple future tense (will finish). The passive structure for simple future is 'will + be + past participle'. Option B correctly includes the agent 'by her' and maintains the original tense and meaning. Option A is grammatically correct but omits the agent. Given the options, B is a more complete transformation.
questions.hint: Identify the tense of the original sentence and apply the passive voice structure accordingly.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice transformation for the given sentence: 'The students completed the assignment on time.'

options.text: The assignment is completed by the students on time.
options.explanation: This uses the present simple passive voice, which is incorrect for the given sentence.

options.text: The assignment was completed by the students on time.
options.explanation: This correctly transforms the active sentence into the passive voice using the simple past tense.

options.text: The assignment had been completed by the students on time.
options.explanation: This uses the past perfect tense, which is not appropriate for the given sentence.

options.text: The assignment will be completed by the students on time.
options.explanation: This uses the future simple passive voice, which is incorrect for the given sentence.

questions.explanation: The original sentence is in the simple past active voice (Subject + V2 + Object). The passive voice for simple past is (Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject).
questions.hint: Identify the tense of the original sentence and apply the passive voice structure for simple past.

questions.question: Identify the correct passive voice for the sentence: 'Someone will deliver the parcel tomorrow.'

options.text: The parcel is delivered tomorrow by someone.
options.explanation: This uses the present simple passive voice, which is incorrect for the given sentence.

options.text: The parcel was delivered tomorrow by someone.
options.explanation: This uses the simple past passive voice, which is incorrect for the given sentence.

options.text: The parcel will be delivered tomorrow.
options.explanation: This correctly transforms the active sentence into the passive voice using the simple future tense. The agent 'by someone' is omitted as it is general.

options.text: The parcel would be delivered tomorrow by someone.
options.explanation: This uses the future in the past passive voice, which is incorrect for the given sentence.

questions.explanation: The original sentence is in the simple future active voice (Subject + will + V1 + Object). The passive voice is (Object + will be + V3 + by + Subject). 'By someone' is usually omitted in passive voice when the agent is unknown or unimportant.
questions.hint: Identify the tense of the original sentence and apply the passive voice structure for simple future.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct passive voice of 'Do your homework'?

options.text: Let your homework be done.
options.explanation: This is the most direct and common passive transformation for the imperative sentence 'Do your homework'.

options.text: Your homework should be done.
options.explanation: This is a possible passive transformation but not the most direct one for a simple command.

options.text: You are ordered to do your homework.
options.explanation: This is not a direct passive transformation of the given imperative sentence.

options.text: Your homework is done by you.
options.explanation: This is not a correct passive transformation of the given imperative sentence.

questions.explanation: For imperative sentences (commands), the passive voice often begins with 'Let' followed by the object and 'be + V3'. Options B and C are also possible depending on context, but A is the most direct and common transformation for a simple command.
questions.hint: Imperative sentences in passive voice often start with 'Let'.
questions.subject: cbse12-english

questions.question: Transform the sentence into passive voice: 'We must help the poor.'

options.text: The poor are to be helped by us.
options.explanation: This is a possible passive transformation but not the most direct one using the modal verb 'must'.

options.text: The poor should be helped by us.
options.explanation: This uses 'should' instead of 'must', which changes the meaning of the original sentence.

options.text: The poor must be helped by us.
options.explanation: This correctly transforms the active sentence into the passive voice using the modal verb 'must'.

options.text: The poor were helped by us.
options.explanation: This uses the simple past passive voice, which is incorrect for the given sentence.

questions.explanation: When a modal verb (like 'must') is used in the active voice, its passive form is 'modal + be + V3'. The modal verb must be retained.
questions.hint: Identify the modal verb in the sentence and apply the passive voice structure for modal verbs.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive transformation for the interrogative sentence: 'Who painted this magnificent portrait?'

options.text: By whom was this magnificent portrait painted?
options.explanation: This correctly transforms the interrogative sentence into the passive voice by changing 'Who' to 'By whom' and placing the auxiliary verb before the subject.

options.text: Who was this magnificent portrait painted by?
options.explanation: This is not the correct structure for a passive interrogative sentence.

options.text: By whom this magnificent portrait was painted?
options.explanation: This is not a grammatically correct passive interrogative sentence.

options.text: This magnificent portrait was painted by whom?
options.explanation: This is a passive statement, not an interrogative sentence.

questions.explanation: When 'Who' is the subject in an interrogative active sentence, it changes to 'By whom' in the passive voice, and the auxiliary verb precedes the object.
questions.hint: In passive voice interrogative sentences, 'Who' changes to 'By whom', and the auxiliary verb comes before the subject.

questions.question: Transform the following sentence into passive voice: 'The children laughed at the joker.'

options.text: The joker was laughed by the children.

options.text: The joker had been laughed at by the children.

questions.hint: Identify the phrasal verb in the sentence and retain the preposition in the passive voice.

questions.question: Identify the sentence that is in the passive voice.

questions.question: Read the following sentence from a literary review: 'Critics generally consider 'Moby Dick' to be one of the greatest American novels.' Choose the correct passive transformation of the underlined part of the sentence.

options.text: 'Moby Dick' is generally considered by critics to be one of the greatest American novels.
options.explanation: This is grammatically correct but less concise as it includes the agent 'by critics'.

options.text: 'Moby Dick' generally considers to be one of the greatest American novels.
options.explanation: This is grammatically incorrect as it changes the meaning and structure of the sentence.

options.text: 'Moby Dick' is generally considered to be one of the greatest American novels.
options.explanation: This correctly transforms the active sentence into the passive voice by making 'Moby Dick' the subject and omitting the agent 'by critics'.

options.text: One of the greatest American novels is generally considered 'Moby Dick' by critics.
options.explanation: This is grammatically incorrect and does not correctly transform the sentence into passive voice.

questions.explanation: The active voice part is 'Critics generally consider 'Moby Dick' to be...'. Here, 'Moby Dick' is the object which becomes the subject in the passive voice. The structure for such sentences is often 'Subject + is/are + V3 + to be...'. The agent 'by critics' can be omitted as it's general.
questions.hint: Identify the object in the active sentence and make it the subject in the passive voice.
questions.subject: cbse12-english
